$comment: ★★ DSS's OWN COMMON BESIDE cl's SELECT-ANY DEFINITION OF ITS NAME: THE DEFINITION REPLACES THE COMMON (P69 fold 3b; D-C-TENTATIVE-DEFINITIONS-OF-ONE-NAME-IN-TWO-UNITS-REFUSED) -- `examples/c/common_beside_a_selectany_definition_pe` with the COMMON written by DSS: main.c's `int dss_tentative;` is a tentative definition, which a unit compiled for a document that states commons writes as a COMMON, as cl writes every one of its own. The one object named to the link is cl's build of `__declspec(selectany) int dss_tentative = 5;`, a COMDAT select-any DEFINITION. The PE documents' `commonYieldsTo: nonOverridableDefinition` makes it replace the common, and the program reads 5, exit 42 -- the answer link.exe and lld-link give cl's own common beside the same object (✔MEASURED 2026-10-08, both orders). Before P69 fold 3b the unit wrote `dss_tentative` as a zero-filled STRONG definition in `.bss`, and a select-any definition yields to a strong one: the program read 0, exit 37. The `release` arm pins that optimizing the unit keeps the common.
